question: In Lithuania, the National Audit Office has issued its findings on the work of the Ministry of Agriculture. According to the National Audit Office, ‘the agricultural sector should be more actively involved as social partners in the work of working groups set up to address policy-making issues. [...] The Ministry does not have criteria regarding when and which social partners should be involved in working groups.

49% of the associations surveyed consider that the process of coordinating legislation with the social partners does not take place, and 46% of the respondents indicated that the process is flawed. This means that the social partners are not able to participate sufficiently in the legislative process or to make proposals at all stages of the legislative process’1.

Based on these findings, the Ministry of Agriculture has infringed Article 106(3) of Regulation 2021/2115 in the preparation of the Lithuanian Strategic Plan: ‘3. Each Member State shall organise a partnership with the competent regional and local authorities.

The partnership shall include at least the following partners: […] (b) economic and social partners, including representatives of the agricultural sector; [...] Member States shall effectively involve those partners in the preparation of the CAP Strategic Plans and shall consult with relevant stakeholders, including as regards the minimum standards referred to in Article 13, where appropriate’.
Could the Commission please answer the following questions: 1.
Is the Commission aware of these findings?
Will the Commission require Lithuania to seek input from all farmers’ organisations on the CAP Strategic Plan, prepare amendments to it and submit it to the Commission for coordination?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.3.2024) The Commission understands that the findings of the Lithuanian National Audit Office (on the involvement of the agricultural sector in policy making) are addressed to the Lithuanian Ministry of Agriculture. The Commission cannot comment on findings from a report under exclusive national responsibility, which it has not received in an official capacity.

Under Article 106 of Regulation (EU) 2021/21151, it is the responsibility of each Member State to organise a partnership for both drawing up and accompanying the implementation the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan.

This partnership should be organised and implemented in line with the provisions of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 240/20142, which requires Member States to ensure that the partners selected are the most representative of the relevant stakeholders, with no obligation to include all of them.
Furthermore, the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 240/2014 does not limit the process of consultations of relevant partners to working groups only.

After approval, the implementation of the CAP Strategic Plans and proposals for amendments shall be examined by the CAP Strategic Plan monitoring committee established under Article 124 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115, that brings together the relevant public authorities and intermediate bodies and representatives of the partners referred to in Article 106(3) of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115.

The Commission participates in the monitoring committee in an advisory capacity and has no role in coordination of stakeholders’ inputs. Alongside the formal partnership structures, the Commission encourages Member States to actively involve interested stakeholders in the implementation of the CAP Strategic Plans.
